sections.normalized_html:
To write a two-digit number (greater than [MATH: 20]) in words, we

  • write the tens part, followed by a hyphen

  • then, write the ones part.

Let's write down the place values of [MATH: 81\mathbin{:}]

tens

ones

[MATH: \color{blue}8]

[MATH: \color{red}1]

Now, we write the number in words:

  • The number has [MATH: \color{blue}8] tens, so we write "eighty," followed by a hyphen:

    [MATH: \qquad]"eighty-"

  • The number has [MATH: \color{red}1] ones, so we add "one":

    [MATH: \qquad] "eighty-one"

Therefore, the number [MATH: 81] written in words is eighty-one.

Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
In this lesson, we'll learn how to write numbers up to eight digits in words. We start by considering two-digit numbers.

Content:
Suppose we want to write the number [MATH: 56] in words. We start by writing down its place value chart.

Content:
| tens | ones |
| [MATH: \color{blue}5] | [MATH: \color{red}6] |

Content:
Now, we write the number in words as follows:

Content:
- The number has [MATH: \color{blue}5] tens, so we write "fifty," followed by a hyphen:

[MATH: \qquad] "fifty-"
- The number has [MATH: \color{red}6] ones, so we add "six":

[MATH: \qquad] "fifty-six"

Content:
Therefore, the number [MATH: 56] written in words is fifty-six.

Content:
Watch Out! Don't forget to include the hyphen!
